newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end firm, Andina climbs.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end firm, Andina climbs.

text.p: Chilean stocks closed broadly stronger in thin trade with soft drinks bottler Andina rallying 10 percent, said traders.
The bolsa is expected to remain steady at the opening with no news seen most heavyweight stocks, said Guillermo Tagle, head of research at Santander Investment.
"We don't see any reason for a change in trend in the current atmosphere," said Tagle.
The 40-share index closed up 0.16 percent at 136.21 points. The general index firmed 0.03 percent to 5,837.08 points.
Turnover slumped to 10 billion pesos from 12.5 billion pesos Monday.
Traders noted the bolsa was weakened by profit-taking with sentiment dampened by news that Salomon Brothers had downgraded Chile in its Latin American portfolio.
Salomon cut Chile to 9.8 percent from 11.8 percent, citing high stock valuations after the recent rally.
Andina led the market winners, with the stock climbing 10 percent to 1,650 pesos.
Analysts said there were no clear reasons for Andina's surge, but added that the stock was probably boosted by short-term buying and could slip back in the next few days.
"It's curious. There's no fundamental reason, as far as I know, for the rise," said Tagle.
Other gainers included power giant Endesa, up 1.57 percent at 323 pesos and its parent company Enersis which gained 0.98 percent at 308 pesos.
Losers included telecom Entel, down 2.03 percent at 3,130 pesos and pulp-maker Copec which shed 1.64 percent at 2,105 pesos.
